relationships.subject: heme
relationships.evidence_quote: Heme treatment led to a time-dependent increase in the characteristic features of sickle pain (mechanical and thermal hyperalgesia) in both sickle and control mice

relationships.subject: TLR4
relationships.evidence_quote: TLR4 deletion in sickle mice attenuated chronic and hypoxia/reoxygenation (H/R)-evoked acute hyperalgesia.

relationships.subject: resatorvid (TAK242)
relationships.evidence_quote: Sickle mice treated with the TLR4 inhibitor resatorvid; selective small-molecule inhibitor of TLR4 (TAK242) had significantly reduced chronic hyperalgesia

relationships.subject: TLR4
relationships.evidence_quote: TLR4 inhibition in spinal cord microglial cells attenuated heme-induced ROS and ER stress

relationships.subject: salubrinal
relationships.evidence_quote: reducing ER stress with salubrinal ameliorated chronic hyperalgesia in sickle mice

key_findings: Heme acts via TLR4 to drive ROS, ER stress and spinal microglial activation causing sickle pain
TLR4 knockout or inhibition and ER stress reduction relieve hyperalgesia in sickle mice
